title: Board discretion to find a proposed Manager of Record unsuitable
subtopic: Suitability of a proposed Manager of Record
rule_summary: In its discretion the Board may determine a PROPOSED MANAGER OF RECORD is not suitable to MANAGE a pharmacy, and that it would not be in the interest of public health, safety, and welfare to approve the application for a change of Manager of Record. The TEN listed factors all describe the proposed Manager of Record: acting in a manner that presented an immediate or serious threat to public health and safety; preventing or attempting to impede the work of a representative of the Board or the Department or the lawful enforcement of M.G.L. c. 112, M.G.L. c. 94C or regulations under them; having OWNED, OPERATED, HELD AN INTEREST IN OR MANAGED a pharmacy, healthcare facility or other FDA- or DEA-registered entity that was the subject of proceedings resulting in discipline, suspension, denial or revocation of the pharmacy license or other professional license or registration; having owned, operated, held an interest in or managed such an entity that entered into a consent agreement in resolution of a complaint resulting in disciplinary action against the pharmacy license or other professional license or registration; having owned, operated, held an interest in or managed such an entity in a manner that created an immediate or serious threat to public health and safety; failure to demonstrate the competence or experience to MANAGE a pharmacy; obtaining or attempting to obtain a license by fraud or misrepresentation, including the submission of false information; HAVING BEEN DISCIPLINED BY THE BOARD WITHIN FIVE YEARS of the date of the application; having held a professional license or registration that was the subject of proceedings resulting in discipline, suspension, denial or revocation; and having entered into a consent agreement in resolution of a complaint against a professional license or registration resulting in disciplinary action against that license or registration.
exam_relevance: Tests that the Board's discretion on a change-of-Manager-of-Record application runs under its own list rather than the 247 CMR 6.03 licensure factors, adding discipline by the Board within five years and omitting the prescriptive-privileges and circumvention-of-ownership factors.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations

numeric_facts.fact: Look-back for discipline by the Board as a listed factor
numeric_facts.conditions: measured from the date of the change-of-Manager-of-Record application

common_confusions: Reaching for the 247 CMR 6.03 licensure factors on a change-of-Manager-of-Record application: 247 CMR 6.10(3) is the list that governs it.
Assuming the two lists match: 247 CMR 6.10(3) adds discipline by the Board within five years of the application and contains no prescriptive-privileges factor.
Overlooking that 247 CMR 6.10(3) also counts an entity the proposed Manager merely managed, which 247 CMR 6.03 does not name.
verification_notes: Read in the current official text of 247 CMR 6.00: Licensure of Pharmacies published at mass.gov on 2026-09-11. Added as a new rule so that no released adjudication is disturbed.
